auto.security_description: Manage Web access authentication, SSH host trust, passwords, tokens, and configuration encryption.
auto.ssh_host_trust_hint: The first connection asks you to verify the host fingerprint. If a saved fingerprint changes, a red warning lets you trust it once, update the record, or cancel.
auto.trusted_hosts_hint: Hosts appear here after the first SSH connection.
auto.local_direct_hint: “Direct local access” requires both the source and Host to be loopback or a current machine address, with no reverse-proxy forwarding headers. Access through a LAN address, reverse-proxy domain, or forwarded proxy still requires sign-in.
auto.trusted_proxy_hint: Only requests from these IPs may use X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. Automatic mode sends Secure cookies only for direct HTTPS or when a trusted proxy explicitly reports HTTPS.
auto.local_desktop_integration: Allow direct local browsers to use desktop integration automatically
auto.local_desktop_integration_hint: Disabled by default. When enabled, X Server and system remote clients are exposed only if Terma listens exclusively on loopback, the browser connects directly from this computer, and the current Web access policy is satisfied.
auto.allowed_hosts_hint: Nothing is required for direct access through localhost, the current machine name, or a listen IP. For a custom reverse-proxy domain, enter the exact Host used by the browser; wildcards are not supported.
auto.login_protection_hint: Per-source protection affects only the current source address. Global protection briefly pauses new sign-in attempts after failures accumulate across multiple sources. Disabling global protection does not disable per-source protection.
auto.lan_password_warning: Without a LAN password, devices on the same network may directly operate SSH, SFTP, keys, tunnels, and batch commands.
auto.session_hint: Changes apply to new sessions immediately. Reducing the lifetime or session limit also tightens existing sessions; expired sessions cannot continue even before the next scheduled cleanup.
auto.web_password_hint: The Web password is used for browser sign-in. It is normally all you need for regular use, phone access, and LAN access.
auto.access_token_hint: The token is mainly for scripts, curl, or third-party tools that call the API with a Bearer token. It can also be entered on the sign-in page when authentication is required and no Web password is set. Tokens are generated randomly and shown only once.
auto.config_encryption_hint: Configuration encryption is not required for normal use. When enabled, saved private-key paths and extra SSH options are encrypted; private-key files themselves are not. Personal and LAN-only deployments can usually leave it disabled.
auto.config_encryption_detail: When enabled, SSH connections, SFTP, terminals, tunnels, and batch commands must unlock encrypted fields before use. Legacy encryption rotates to a new key after the old master password is entered; create a new backup and remove old v1 backups afterward. Disabling encryption requires the master password and decrypts the protected database fields.

theme.title: Interface effects
theme.frosted_scope: Dialogs, menus, and the SFTP shell; increase for a softer appearance
theme.luminous_scope: Activity bar, explorer, top navigation, and notifications; increase for more visible motion
theme.frosted_help: Controls background blur and surface separation. Higher values soften dialogs and tool layers; lower values preserve background detail and reduce work on lower-performance devices.
theme.luminous_help: Controls transparency, saturation, edge highlights, shadows, and slowly moving reflection bands. Higher values make the material clearer and more layered; lower values make it resemble a stable translucent panel.
theme.compatibility_note: Luminous glass is still being adapted. Terminal content, text editors, diffs, and some system controls remain solid to preserve clarity and compatibility.
